title: Assign Cookies
prompt: You are given two integer arrays `g` and `s`, where `g[i]` is the greed factor of the `i`-th child (the minimum size cookie that child will be content with), and `s[j]` is the size of the `j`-th cookie. Each cookie can satisfy at most one child, and a child is content only if given a cookie of size greater than or equal to their greed factor. Return the maximum number of children you can make content.

examples.explanation: With only cookies of size 1, you can satisfy at most the child with greed factor 1.
You have 3 cookies and 2 children. You can satisfy both children.

hints: Trying every child-cookie pairing is wasteful — think about what order to hand out cookies in.
Sort both the greed factors and the cookie sizes.

Use two pointers: give the least greedy unsatisfied child the smallest cookie big enough for them. If the current cookie can't satisfy the current child, no smaller cookie could either, so move to a bigger cookie; if it can, both pointers advance.

solution.approach: Sort both arrays. Walk through cookies in increasing size, and greedily assign the smallest available cookie to the least greedy child it can satisfy. If the current cookie is too small for the current child, it's too small for every remaining (greedier) child too, so skip to the next cookie. If it satisfies the child, count it and advance both pointers. This greedy matching is optimal because using the smallest sufficient cookie on the least demanding unsatisfied child never wastes capacity that a greedier child could have used instead.
solution.timeComplexity: O(n log n + m log m)
